container-queries.headline: Components that respond to their own space.
container-queries.explanation: Container queries let a component adapt to its available width instead of relying on the viewport.
container-queries.demoTitle: A little room for good ideas.
container-queries.demoDescription: A comfortable corner. A fresh perspective. Somewhere to stay curious.

fluid-type.headline: A little space. A different scale.
fluid-type.explanation: Container units and clamp() let type grow with its surroundings while keeping a comfortable minimum and maximum size. Resize the card to see its headline scale.
fluid-type.demoTitle: Good ideas grow with a little room.
fluid-type.demoDescription: A comfortable corner. A fresh perspective. Somewhere to stay curious.

aspect-ratio.headline: Give every image room to belong.
aspect-ratio.explanation: Aspect-ratio gives an image a predictable frame. Here, a container query changes that frame from a wide view to a square as the card gains space.
aspect-ratio.demoDescription: A comfortable corner. A fresh perspective. Somewhere to stay curious.

scroll-state.headline: A reading room that knows where you are
scroll-state.explanation: Scroll the reading panel. Its heading stays nearby; supported browsers label it when stuck.
scroll-state.demoTitle: A reading room that knows where you are
scroll-state.demoDescription: The chapter heading stays visible. In supporting browsers, a Reading now label appears while it is stuck to the top edge.

specificity.headline: Which rule gets the last word?
specificity.explanation: Enable a class rule, an ID rule, or both. The stronger selector determines the invitation’s border and message.
specificity.demoTitle: Which rule gets the last word?
specificity.demoDescription: The invitation border and winner label reveal which of the two competing selectors wins.

style-queries.headline: One card, three kinds of welcome
style-queries.explanation: Choose a warm context. A custom property carries that context to the nested invitation.
style-queries.demoTitle: One card, three kinds of welcome
style-queries.demoDescription: A nested invitation changes its spacing and treatment through style queries, with the selected context named in text.

popovers-anchors.headline: A note that stays close
popovers-anchors.explanation: Open the reading note. Click outside or press Escape to dismiss the native popover.
popovers-anchors.demoDescription: The note follows its anchor and demonstrates alternate placements without covering the trigger.

page-transitions.headline: Follow a good idea from room to room
page-transitions.explanation: Switch between the collection and reading views. View Transitions connects the two states when available.
page-transitions.demoTitle: Follow a good idea from room to room
page-transitions.demoDescription: The collection changes into a reading preview, with a shared named view and a native transition when supported.

modern-resets.headline: The same content, a better starting point
modern-resets.explanation: Compare content-box with border-box. Both frames request the same width and padding.
modern-resets.demoTitle: The same content, a better starting point
modern-resets.demoDescription: The box changes how it accounts for padding and borders; heading margins and the native control font adopt a minimal baseline.

subgrid.headline: Everything finds its line
subgrid.explanation: Toggle shared tracks. The longer description shows why nested cards benefit from subgrid.
subgrid.demoDescription: Titles, descriptions and reading links align across nested cards even when their copy lengths differ.

text-margin-trim.headline: See the space around the letters
text-margin-trim.explanation: Toggle text-edge trimming and compare the line boxes against the specimen borders. The current CSS property is text-box-trim.
text-margin-trim.demoTitle: See the space around the letters
text-margin-trim.demoDescription: The trimmed specimen sits flush with its intended text edges while the untrimmed line box remains visible alongside it.

flex-safe.headline: A welcome that never slips out of reach
flex-safe.explanation: Add more invitations, then choose safe centering. Overflow should begin where the first item stays reachable.
flex-safe.demoTitle: A welcome that never slips out of reach
flex-safe.demoDescription: Short rows stay centered; overflowing rows align from the start so the first item remains reachable.

color-mix.headline: Build a palette from one warm note
color-mix.explanation: Adjust the amber proportion. Compare two real CSS color spaces; the labels stay readable independently of the swatches.
color-mix.demoTitle: Build a palette from one warm note
color-mix.demoDescription: Two swatches respond to the same amber proportion, showing the difference between sRGB and OKLCH mixing.

smart-selectors.headline: Let the card describe its context
smart-selectors.explanation: Include a cover image. :has() notices the content; :is() groups matching elements and :where() keeps the baseline selector gentle.
smart-selectors.demoTitle: Let the card describe its context
smart-selectors.demoDescription: Adding a cover changes the border through :has(); the CSS shows :is() grouping and a low-specificity :where() baseline.

calc-size.headline: A little more than auto
calc-size.explanation: Ask for extra room around an intrinsically sized note. Supported browsers calculate from auto instead of guessing a fixed height.
calc-size.demoDescription: The expanded frame follows its content and demonstrates a calculated amount of extra room instead of a guessed fixed height.

the-layer-rule.headline: Set the order, settle the cascade
the-layer-rule.explanation: Compare two declared layer orders. The selectors are identical in strength; the order of the layers decides the border.
the-layer-rule.demoTitle: Set the order, settle the cascade
the-layer-rule.demoDescription: The winning style changes with layer precedence, accompanied by a short explanation of the rule that won.

transition-behavior.headline: A goodbye with a little grace
transition-behavior.explanation: Show and hide the note. Supporting browsers coordinate opacity with the discrete display change.
transition-behavior.demoTitle: A goodbye with a little grace
transition-behavior.demoDescription: Opacity and discrete display changes cooperate so the panel can enter and leave smoothly without timeout-based removal.

sibling-index.headline: A whole list, one motion budget
sibling-index.explanation: Switch between seven and forty notes and replay the decorative entrance. Every line of text is readable immediately.
sibling-index.demoTitle: A whole list, one motion budget
sibling-index.demoDescription: Only the first few items stagger; a capped delay keeps the final warning visible promptly in both batches.
